original_value: Huge data on the web come from discussion forums, which contain millions of threads. Discussion threads are a valuable source of knowledge for Internet users, as they have information about numerous topics. The discussion thread related to single topic comprises a huge number of reply posts, which makes it hard for the forum users to scan all the replies and determine the most relevant replies in the thread. At the same time, it is also hard for the forum users to manually summarize the bulk of reply posts in order to get the gist of discussion thread. Thus, automatically extracting the most relevant replies from discussion thread and combining them to form a summary are a challenging task. With this motivation behind, this study has proposed a sentence embedding based clustering approach for discussion thread summarization. The proposed approach works in the following fashion: At first, word2vec model is employed to represent reply sentences in the discussion thread through sentence embeddings/sentence vectors. Next, K-medoid clustering algorithm is applied to group semantically similar reply sentences in order to reduce the overlapping reply sentences. Finally, different quality text features are utilized to rank the reply sentences in different clusters, and then the high-ranked reply sentences are picked out from all clusters to form the thread summary. Two standard forum datasets are used to assess the effectiveness of the suggested approach. Empirical results confirm that the proposed sentence based clustering approach performed superior in comparison to other summarization methods in the context of mean precision, recall, and F-measure.

result.paraphrase: Discussion forums make up a large share of web data and contain millions of threads. Because these threads cover many topics, they are an important knowledge source for Internet users. A thread on a single topic can include a very large number of reply posts, making it difficult for users to review every reply and identify the most relevant ones. It is also hard to manually condense the many replies into a concise summary that captures the main point of the discussion. For this reason, automatically selecting the most relevant replies from a discussion thread and combining them into a summary is a challenging task. Motivated by this problem, the study proposes a sentence-embedding-based clustering method for discussion-thread summarization. The approach works as follows: first, a word2vec model is used to represent reply sentences as sentence embeddings, or sentence vectors, in the discussion thread. Next, the K-medoid clustering algorithm groups semantically similar reply sentences to reduce redundancy. Finally, various quality text features are used to rank the reply sentences within each cluster, and the top-ranked sentences from all clusters are selected to create the thread summary. Two standard forum datasets are used to evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed approach. Experimental results show that the sentence-based clustering method outperformed other summarization methods in terms of mean precision, recall, and F-measure.
